text:
Maria G: FYI staging apply failed during rollout of `module/ingress` — plan shows drift + state lock errors. anyone around to help?
Alex K: on it. can you paste the `terraform plan` snippet or the error?
Maria G: here — getting two errors: `Error: resource changed outside of Terraform` for k8s_service.account, and `Error acquiring the state lock` with lock ID set to a DynamoDB item.
Maria G: ```
Error: resource changed outside of Terraform
  on k8s/ingress.tf line 12, in resource "kubernetes_service_account" "external_dns":
  │ The resource in the state differs from the real-world object...

Error acquiring the state lock: ResourceNotFoundException: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
```
Alex K: ok. two paths: 1) if someone is actively applying, don't force-unlock. if not, we can `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` after verifying no active applies.
Jia L: I checked CI — no running applies. lock TTL is old (created ~30m ago). go ahead with unlock but let's capture the lock item first.
Sam R: +1. Steps I'd take: `terraform state pull > state.json` then `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "<LOCK_ID>"}}'` to verify.
Maria G: LOCK_ID is `abc-123-staging-ingress`. I grabbed state earlier and uploaded to the runbook.
Alex K: also, the drift on the SA probably because external process `kubectl apply` created an annotation. We can import the resource to match live state or update the live object to match tf. Which do we prefer?
Jia L: prefer import if live state is canonical (this time it is — external dns has extra annotation from cert-manager). do: `terraform import module.ingress.kubernetes_service_account.external_dns default/external-dns`
Sam R: note: provider version mismatch can make attributes appear changed. what does `terraform providers` show?
Maria G: running now: `hashicorp/kubernetes v2.14.0` on local machine, while staging uses `v2.11.0` from the lock file.
Alex K: that explains the attribute diffs. After unlock and import, run `terraform plan -refresh=true -var-file=staging.tfvars` from the pipeline image to get consistent provider.
Terraform Bot: Reminder: do not run `force-unlock` while an apply is in progress. Use `terraform force-unlock -force abc-123-staging-ingress` only after confirming no active ops.
Maria G: I'll do the sequence: capture dynamo item, force-unlock, import SA, then `plan`. tagging @Alex K so you can watch the apply.
Alex K: Sounds good. also check for any tainted resources: `terraform state list | grep taint` and `terraform taint -list` (depending on TF version).
Jia L: small gotcha — when importing k8s resources via the provider, the import id format depends on resource: for `kubernetes_service_account` it's `namespace/name`. you already used `default/external-dns` which is correct.
Sam R: If plan still shows drift after import, run `terraform state show module.ingress.kubernetes_service_account.external_dns` and compare to `kubectl -n default get sa external-dns -o yaml`.
Maria G: Unlock done, import succeeded, plan now shows only the annotation difference (cert-manager). I'm going to update the tf to accept the annotation via `metadata { annotations = {"cert-manager.io/...." = "present"} }` and run apply.
Alex K: great — if that change is just metadata it's safe. after apply, push a small commit to pin provider version to v2.14.0 in the module to avoid repeat drift.
Maria G: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
Terraform Bot: Apply queued: staging/ingress by Maria G. Run ID: r-20260322-42
Jia L: nice work. quick note for runbook: add a checklist for stale dynamodb locks + import pattern. saved me an hour last week.
Sam R: adding to runbook now. entry: `verify no active apply -> capture lock -> force-unlock -> import resource -> refresh plan -> apply`
Maria G: closing the thread after apply completes. thanks everyone.
